sender.en: A brand or online store advertised on Facebook or Instagram

name.en: Fake online store: huge discounts, goods never arrive or are counterfeit

how.en: Ads on social media lead to websites that copy real brands and offer huge discounts, such as 80% off, with phrases like “Today only”. Fraudsters also sell items or event tickets on marketplaces that never arrive. You pay and get nothing, or get a poor counterfeit that may even be unsafe. Big events like the FIFA World Cup bring fake tickets, travel packages and look-alike stores.

text.en: You see an ad with a huge discount from a store or brand.
It says the sale is “today only” or stock is limited.
The link goes to a look-alike website or a recently created seller profile.
You pay, and the goods never arrive or are fake.
CLOSING SALE – everything 80% OFF today only! Premium boots now $39.99. Free shipping across Canada. Shop now before stock runs out: [link]

en: Spelling mistakes, or the product called “the item”.
Sellers with new social media profiles or no reviews outside the site.
Know the normal price and look for reviews on other sites.
Pay by credit card, which offers fraud protection.
Buy event tickets only from the official seller.
If you paid, contact your card provider, then report it to the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre.
